title: Finland's 2027 Budget Bets on Growth While Deficit and Joblessness Linger · 07 Sep
keywords: Finland, budget 2027, fiscal deficit, unemployment, corporate tax cuts, eurozone, European Commission, economic recovery, Finnish politics, public finances, labor market, EU fiscal rules
notes: Finland's coalition government has unveiled a 2027 budget combining corporate tax cuts with continued spending reductions, framing the package as evidence of an economy turning a corner. But European Commission projections place the general government deficit at 4.6 percent of GDP in 2027, and unemployment is forecast to remain near 10 percent, figures that sit uneasily alongside the government's recovery narrative. The gap between official optimism and measurable economic strain is sharpening political debate in Helsinki and drawing scrutiny from Brussels.
